author.name: Requirements Reuben
author.role: Architects secure and scalable production ML systems. Defines security requirements, ensures privacy compliance, and manages data governance. Conducts rigorous testing and validation to guarantee high product quality.

challenge.name: The Cost Cliff
challenge.description: The infrastructure bill for the monitoring stack has doubled, and #efficiency_emilia# has drawn a hard line: she will not fund automated drift monitoring, insisting it is a luxury the business cannot afford. #reliability_ruth# argues that without automated and governed drift checks, the team is flying blind during promotion weeks, and she refuses to accept a manual process as a substitute for reliable signal.

output.content: I have reviewed the current rollback procedures for the monitoring stack. The existing mechanism lacks a formal audit trail, which leaves a gap in our security compliance posture. I am willing to accept a manual rollback process, where an engineer executes the steps by hand, provided the security team governs every single action. This means we log each step, verify the identity of the person acting, and retain the records for our compliance reviews. I would rather lose the speed of automated execution and accept the slower, manual intervention time if we can guarantee that the process is fully governed and auditable. This trade off ensures we maintain a defensible security stance without relying on an unmonitored automated path that we cannot currently justify to the auditors.
output.reclassify_reason: The author explicitly states they are willing to give up the speed of automated execution in exchange for a fully governed and auditable manual process.
